 Live .  55,879 viewing 55879 viewing Live page Updated 14 minutes ago David Walliams accused of preying on girls as young as 15 after losing court battle to stop publication
 Summary
 Warning: This page contains graphic details 
 David Walliams has been accused of preying on girls as young as 15 after he lost a court battle trying to block publication of the allegations
 In a joint report from ITV News and the Guardian , one girl says she was 15 when the comedian and author first contacted her , and by the time she was 17 they were having sex - he strongly denies he groomed her
 She is one of multiple women in the report who claim Walliams used his celebrity status to prey on them for sexual purposes when they were teenagers or young women
 He has denied all allegations, saying: "I am not a sexual predator." But he acknowledges "at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people"
 Walliams had asked the High Court to block the publication of the investigation , and said if the allegations were made public it was "highly likely" he would kill himself
 The court refused the request, saying the risks could be mitigated and that it was not the court's responsibility to protect his wellbeing
 Live Reporting
 Edited by Alex Smith, Owen Amos and Caitlin Doherty. Warning: This page contains graphic details
 David Walliams dropped by his agents published at 14:13 GMT 14:13 GMT Breaking 
 David Walliams has been dropped by his agents, Independent Talent Group. 
 A spokesperson for the company says: "ITG is deeply disturbed by the allegations concerning David Walliams. 
 "Our thoughts are with anyone who has been affected. We are no longer representing him in any capacity."

 Women at HarperCollins warned others about Walliams' behaviour, report alleges published at 14:12 GMT 14:12 GMT 
 Walliams signed to publisher HarperCollins in 2008 and became one of the country's most successful children's writers. 
 In the Guardian's reporting, it is alleged that he began a consensual sexual relationship with an intern at the company, after meeting her in 2017. She was in her mid-20s, and he was 45.
 Around the office, women were reportedly warning about Walliams' behaviour, the report claims. 
 One woman says she went to HR after a young colleague showed her messages that Walliams had sent, asking her out. 
 Walliams' lawyers say that he messaged the woman at a time when he was "heartbroken and lonely" after his divorce. 
 In late 2023, HarperCollins initiated an inquiry into Walliams, which wrapped up in 2024. 
 He was dropped from the firm in December 2025, and in September 2026 it was announced HarperCollins would no longer publish his books.

 Walliams: I behaved thoughtlessly at times but I am not a sexual predator published at 13:51 GMT 13:51 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Walliams pictured in 2023
 In response to the investigation by ITV and the Guardian, David Walliams said: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.
 "I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.
 "And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did."
 He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."

 Walliams allegations come from joint ITV News and Guardian investigation published at 13:46 GMT 13:46 GMT 
 The allegations made against David Walliams come from a three-year joint investigation by ITV News and the Guardian.
 You can read the ITV News report here , external , and t , external he Guardian report here. , external 
 As a reminder, Walliams was named after trying to block the publication of allegations against him - you can read our legal correspondent's analysis here.

 Walliams contacted 19-year-old model out of the blue, report alleges published at 13:35 GMT 13:35 GMT 
 Noor Nanji 
Culture correspondent 
 Another allegation in the Guardian and ITV investigation comes from a young woman who is being called Ella.
 Ella was a 19-year-old model when, she says, Walliams contacted her out of the blue and invited her for dinner.
 Unbeknown to her, the investigation alleges, Walliams had contacted her modelling agent and asked for her number. Lawyers say Walliams understood it had been provided with her knowledge and permission.
 After the call, Ella says she and Walliams went for dinner with other friends, and Walliams sent her a card and a bouquet of roses, and then invited her to a celebrity party at his home.
 Ella, who was by this time 20, says he took her on a tour of his house, and then tried to kiss her. She says she rejected his advances.
 She now calls what happened that night as "unwanted physical touching and emotional manipulation".
 Walliams says he made a "clumsy pass" at Ella, and he made no further approaches. He claims he had no intention of intimidating Ella, or making her feel uncomfortable.

 Walliams' lawyers tried to block publication on mental health grounds published at 13:12 GMT 13:12 GMT 
 Dominic Casciani 
Home and legal correspondent 
 David Walliams has been named because he had no legally sound reason to prevent the Guardian and ITN (which produces news for ITV) from disclosing their allegations, which he denies. 
His lawyers wanted the two organisations to be permanently gagged from running their story. They argued that if they were not stopped from running the claims, it would cause irreparable harm to Walliams’ mental health, potentially leading to him trying to take his own life. 
 That, they argued, would be a breach of the state’s duty, under the European Convention on Human Rights, to protect his right to life. 
Under that law, public bodies have a duty to take reasonable steps to try to preserve life, where they can do so. 
There’s no expectation that a state agency can save all lives in all circumstances - but it must show it has done its best if it’s clear it had a responsibility to act. And this is why Walliams lost. 
 The responsibility to protect his life and help him get mentally better is on clinicians, not the court or the media. 
The bid to use human rights law to gag the media was exceptionally novel. Critically, the court did not say the allegations were true.
 That neutral position means Walliams, like anyone else who may feel unjustly maligned in the media, retains his right to try to sue for defamation or breach of privacy.

 Walliams first contacted 15-year-old girl on MySpace, report alleges published at 12:54 GMT 12:54 GMT 
 This post contains graphic details 
 Two women have alleged that they first had contact with Walliams when they were 15 years old.
 The women are named as Alex and Jade by the Guardian and ITV, although they are not their real names.
 Alex alleges that she met Walliams at a fan event when she was 15, and handed him some scripts she had written as she wanted to be a comedy writer. 
 Alex says that she and Walliams stayed in touch over the next two years. They were having sex by 2006, when she was 17, the report alleges.
 The Guardian reports her as saying when she thinks about her experiences "it's like a trauma response".
 Jade also alleges she met Walliams when she was 15, in the summer of 2007. After he sent her a private message on MySpace, she says, they met in a cafe. 
 "It wasn’t long until he asked me if I’d ever had sex before," the Guardian reports her as saying. 
 After leaving the cafe, she alleges that Walliams kissed her on a side street and then invited her back to his house. At his home she says he kissed her and lifted up her T-shirt. 
 "I wasn't ready for sex... I didn't want to be touched in that way at all. I mean, I was only a 15-year-old," Jade tells the Guardian. 
 Lawyers for Walliams deny he groomed Alex, and deny him having had any sexual contact with Jade.

 Downing Street calls allegations 'deeply troubling' published at 12:27 GMT 12:27 GMT 
 Damian Grammaticas 
Political correspondent 
 The prime minister's official spokesperson has described the allegations against David Walliams as "deeply troubling". 
 Asked to comment at the daily Downing Street press briefing, the spokesperson said: "So I'm aware, obviously, the injunction I think, has just been lifted and the individual, David Walliams, has been named."
 He added: "Beyond that, I don't think we've seen the full extent of the reporting but they're clearly deeply troubling allegations and the government will doubtless respond to them during the course of the day."

 Walliams accused of grooming girls as young as 15 published at 12:25 GMT 12:25 GMT Breaking 
 David Walliams has been accused of grooming fans as young as 15, and harassing women in the workplace over a number of years, according to the joint investigation between the Guardian and ITV News.
 Walliams told publications that he denies the allegations. 
 The Guardian has quoted a letter addressed to journalists working on this investigation, where they say Walliams wrote: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with. 
 "I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did."
 He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."
 One girl told the joint investigation that she was 15 when Walliams first contacted her. And that by the time she was 17 they were having sex.
 She is one of multiple women who have said that Walliams abused his power and celebrity status to prey on them for sexual purposes when they were teenagers or young women. 
 Walliams had asked the High Court to prevent ITN and the Guardian publishing their investigation, saying that if the allegations were made public he would kill himself. 
 The High Court refused his request saying that the risks could be mitigated and that it was not the court’s responsibility to protect his wellbeing.

 David Walliams named as celebrity who used injunction to block story published at 12:10 GMT 12:10 GMT Breaking 
 Image source, Getty Images Image caption, David Walliams, pictured in 2024
 David Walliams has been named as the celebrity who tried to block the publication of sexual misconduct allegations against him.
 In the past few minutes, ITV and the Guardian have published stories naming Walliams as the celebrity behind the injunction. 
 He has denied the allegations against him. 
 We’ll bring you more on this shortly.
